- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項

- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって

- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)

  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

【Full Story】
## Main Story

Some wins begin with one loud moment. This one began with a big swing and became a controlled night for Hanshin.

On August 16, 2026, at Mazda Stadium, the Hanshin Tigers faced the Hiroshima Toyo Carp.

In the first inning, Teruaki Sato hit a two-run home run to center field. Hanshin quickly took a 2–0 lead.

Hanshin starter Rihito Ihara gave his team a steady start. He pitched five innings, allowed two hits, and gave up one run.

Hiroshima’s only run came in the bottom of the fifth. Elehuris Montero hit a solo home run, cutting the lead to 2–1.

But Hiroshima could not build on that moment. Hanshin added runs in the seventh and eighth innings, creating a much wider gap.

The final score was Hiroshima 1, Hanshin 8.

Hanshin won not only because of its fast start. The team protected its advantage, limited Hiroshima’s response, and added more offense later.

【Point One】
The important detail in the fifth inning was not only that Hiroshima scored, but how. Montero’s home run produced one run, but Hiroshima never turned its response into a larger attack. With Ihara allowing only two hits in five innings, the Carp had no sustained scoring surge.

【Point Two】
Hanshin’s later offense was shared across the lineup. Seishiro Sakamoto drove in a run in the seventh and added a run-scoring double in the eighth. Pinch-hitter Taira Fushimi also delivered a timely hit in the seventh. The win was reinforced by several contributors, not just Sato’s opening home run.
